checks.label: Adding the two squares and finding the square root of the answer gives each diagonal, run and gap from its two sides (a shorter side takes the squares away instead), and the floors, rooms, grid gap and panel are drawn to those lengths

Revise calculating the length of line segments and using Pythagoras' theorem in 2D: a segment between two grid points is so far across and so far up, each the larger number take away the smaller, so (−1, 1) to (4, 3) is 5 across, 2 up and √29, about 5.39, long, and (−2, 1) to (6, 7) is 8 across, 6 up and 10 long

Pythagoras' theorem can be applied to solve 3-dimensional problems: through each box the line is the root of the floor's diagonal squared plus the height squared, the same as all three edges squared and added, so 6 m by 3 m by 2 m is 7 m, 40 by 40 by 70 cm is 90 cm and 2 m by 1 m by 2 m is 3 m

Pythagoras' theorem is only true for right-angled triangles: the frame drawn from its measured diagonal leans, so its corners are not square, and only a frame with square corners has the diagonal the theorem gives

Each puzzle's answer is worked out from its rule: 6.5 m; 8 m by 6 m, the only room on the grid with a 10 m run; 12 m; 10; 90 cm; not square, as 80 cm by 60 cm with square corners gives 100 cm; 1.3 m; 3 m

Each puzzle accepts only its own answer, and each wrong answer it names is the one a slip gives: the sides added, the square left unrooted, the lengths taken away, the squares added for a shorter side, the gridlines followed, the minus sign dropped, the height added on, the floor alone, the three edges added, 1.2 and 50 squared as if they were in one unit; every room 10 m round two walls; each slip but "Can't tell" is shown in the warning colour

Before an answer, nothing in a puzzle's picture gives it away: the length asked for says ?, the room's straight run says ?, no legs or sums on the grid, no line through the box, no square corners beside the frame, which leans too little to judge by eye, the panel's 50 cm not yet in metres, nothing in the warning colour
Every screen, finished, keeps its labels inside the picture and clear of each other and its points inside it, for every answer, right or wrong, wherever the room's corner or the point is put

Every demonstration has finished arriving within 4.5 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion within 2.5 s and a slip within 1 s; parts start at least 0.45 s apart and counted steps at least 0.2 s apart
